function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Here’s a quick rundown of where you can order cake—whether you’re looking for a local bakery, a national chain, or an online delivery service. Pick the option that best fits your needs (price, delivery time, customization, etc.). | Category | What to Look For | Popular Options | Tips | |----------|------------------|-----------------|------| | **Local Bakery** | Fresh, artisanal cakes; often customizable | - Your local bakery (search “cake shop near me”)
- Specialty bakeries (e.g., “artisan cake shop”) | • Call ahead to confirm availability and delivery hours.
• Ask about custom designs or dietary restrictions (gluten‑free, vegan). | | **National Chain** | Consistent quality, nationwide delivery | - **Baker’s Dozen** (if available in your area)
- **Cakes & Co.** (regional chains) | • Check their website for delivery zones and minimum order amounts.
• Look for seasonal specials or bulk discounts. | | **Online Delivery Platforms** | Wide selection from many bakeries; convenient | - **Uber Eats** (search “cakes” or “bakeries”)
- **DoorDash**
- **Postmates**
- **Instacart** (for grocery‑store cakes) | • Use filters to narrow by cuisine, price, or rating.
• Read recent reviews for freshness and packaging. | | **E‑Commerce Sites** | Pre‑made cakes shipped to your door | - **Amazon Fresh** (check “cakes” under groceries)
- **FreshDirect** (if in service area) | • Verify shipping times and temperature control.
• Look for “same‑day” or “next‑day” delivery options. | | **Specialty Online Shops** | Custom designs, themed cakes | - **Etsy** (search “custom cake”)
- **CakeBoss** (specialty cakes) | • Order at least 1–2 weeks in advance for custom designs.
• Confirm shipping insurance for fragile items. | ### How to Choose 1. **Delivery Time** – If you need the cake ASAP, local bakeries or same‑day delivery platforms are best. 2. **Customization** – For personalized designs or dietary restrictions, call the bakery directly or use a platform that allows custom orders. 3. **Price & Quality** – Compare prices, but remember that higher cost often means fresher ingredients or better packaging. 4. **Reviews** – Look at recent customer feedback on Google, Yelp, or the platform’s own rating system. ### Quick Order Checklist - **What type of cake?** (birthday, wedding, gluten‑free, vegan, etc.) - **Size & Quantity** – Make sure the bakery can accommodate your portion size. - **Delivery Address & Time** – Provide clear instructions and confirm the delivery window. - **Payment Method** – Most platforms accept credit cards, PayPal, or Apple Pay; local bakeries may accept cash or card. Happy cake hunting! If you’d like a specific recommendation for your city, just let me know the zip code or city name.
